Definition: a primary preposition; properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of):--above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with. In compounds it retains the same variety of application.
BiblicalUsage: Para means beside, near, with, from — the small word that puts one person next to another. John was a man sent from God, and the Thessalonians received the word not as the word of men but as the word of God, which came from Him and works in those who believe.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that beside is the position of the gospel: the Word comes from beside the Father, and it works in all who receive it as His word.
